# Method and System for Selective Region Processing in Multimedia Files

## Overview

This disclosure describes a video processing method implemented on a mobile terminal, which enables selective processing of specific regions within a video sequence while preserving the temporal characteristics of the original media file. The system allows a user to designate an area of interest in a single reference frame, automatically propagates this selection across all frames of the video, and applies targeted processing to the surrounding regions—producing a new multimedia file with the original timing preserved.

## Detailed Process Description

### Step 1: Decoding the First Multimedia File

The mobile terminal begins by decoding a first multimedia file—typically a video file in a standard compressed format (e.g., MP4, AVI, or similar container formats). Through this decoding process, the terminal extracts multiple frames of image data, referred to as "first pictures," which represent the sequential visual content of the video. Simultaneously, the terminal retrieves the file's associated time parameter, which encodes critical temporal metadata such as frame rate, timestamp information, and playback duration. This time parameter is essential for maintaining synchronization and ensuring that the eventual output file preserves the same temporal behavior as the original.

### Step 2: Receiving User Input to Select a Region of Interest

Once the video has been decoded into its constituent frames, a first processing unit within the mobile terminal is configured to receive a first input operation from the user. This input operation involves the user selecting a specific area or region within any single frame chosen from the decoded first pictures. The selection can be performed through common interaction methods, such as touch gestures, drawing a bounding box, or tapping to define a region of interest (ROI). This user-defined area typically corresponds to an object, subject, or portion of the frame that the user wishes to preserve or treat differently from the rest of the image content.

### Step 3: Identifying Corresponding Regions Across All Frames

After the initial region is selected in the reference frame, a second processing unit takes over to extend this selection throughout the entire video sequence. Using techniques such as object tracking, feature matching, motion estimation, or other computer vision algorithms, the second processing unit analyzes all other frames in the first pictures to locate the corresponding areas that match the originally selected region. These identified corresponding areas are designated as "first areas" and are marked consistently across every frame of the video, ensuring that the region of interest is accurately tracked even as it may shift position, change in scale, or undergo minor transformations due to camera movement or subject motion.

### Step 4: Applying Predetermined Processing to Non-Selected Regions

With the first areas established across all frames, the system proceeds to apply predetermined processing operations exclusively to the regions lying outside these designated first areas. This processing may include operations such as blurring, pixelation, masking, color adjustment, background replacement, or other visual effects, depending on the specific application (e.g., privacy protection, artistic effect, or content emphasis). By selectively processing only the peripheral or background regions while leaving the first areas untouched, the system generates a new set of frames referred to as "second pictures." These second pictures maintain the integrity and clarity of the user-selected subject while modifying the surrounding content according to the specified processing rules.

### Step 5: Encoding the Processed Frames into a New Multimedia File

Finally, an encoding unit takes the multiple frames of second pictures and re-encodes them into a new multimedia file, referred to as the "second multimedia file." Critically, this encoding process utilizes the original time parameter extracted during the initial decoding step, ensuring that the frame rate, timing, and overall playback characteristics of the new file remain consistent with the original first multimedia file. This preservation of temporal fidelity guarantees that the resulting video plays back smoothly and naturally, with no disruption to its intended pacing or synchronization, despite the selective visual modifications that have been applied.

## Summary

Through this coordinated sequence of decoding, user-guided region selection, cross-frame region tracking, selective processing, and re-encoding, the mobile terminal is able to produce a modified video file that intelligently preserves a user-specified area of interest across the entire duration of the clip while applying customized effects to the remaining content—all while maintaining the original temporal structure of the source file. This approach provides a flexible and efficient framework for applications such as privacy masking, subject highlighting, background editing, and other region-specific video enhancement tasks.

# Selective Region Processing for Multimedia Content on Mobile Terminals

## Background

With the rapid proliferation of mobile terminals equipped with multimedia capture and playback capabilities, users increasingly demand more sophisticated tools for editing and processing video content. Traditional multimedia editing approaches typically apply modifications either to an entire video uniformly or require frame-by-frame manual editing—both of which present significant limitations. Uniform processing across an entire frame often fails to meet user needs when only specific regions require modification, while manual frame-by-frame editing is prohibitively time-consuming and impractical for average users, particularly on resource-constrained mobile devices.

There exists a genuine need for privacy protection (such as blurring faces or license plates), selective enhancement (such as sharpening a particular subject while leaving backgrounds untouched), or region-specific masking (such as obscuring sensitive information) that persists consistently throughout an entire video sequence. Existing solutions in the art fail to adequately address the challenge of enabling users to define a region of interest once and have that region automatically and consistently tracked and processed across all frames of a multimedia file, while simultaneously preserving the original playback timing and quality characteristics of the content.

## Summary of the Disclosure

The present disclosure addresses these shortcomings by providing a mobile terminal and associated method for selectively processing regions within multimedia content in an efficient, user-friendly manner. According to the disclosed technique, a multimedia file—such as a video—is first decoded into a plurality of constituent picture frames. This decoding process extracts the individual image frames along with their associated timing information, ensuring that the temporal relationship between frames is preserved and available for later reconstruction.

Once the multimedia file has been decoded, the mobile terminal presents at least one frame to the user, typically through a display interface, allowing the user to visually inspect the content and select a specific region within that frame. This selected region may correspond to any area of interest, such as a face, an object, a background element, or any other portion of the image that the user wishes to modify. The selection may be accomplished through various input mechanisms available on the mobile terminal, including touch-based selection, stylus input, or other pointing mechanisms, enabling the user to define the boundaries of the region with reasonable precision.

Upon receiving the user's region selection in the reference frame, the mobile terminal employs an identification mechanism to automatically locate the corresponding region within each of the remaining picture frames of the decoded multimedia file. This identification process may utilize various image recognition, feature matching, or object tracking algorithms known in the art, allowing the system to account for movement, rotation, scaling, or other transformations of the selected region as it appears across the sequence of frames. By automatically propagating the region selection across all frames, the disclosed method eliminates the need for the user to manually identify and select the region in each individual frame, thereby substantially reducing the time and effort required for the editing task.

Following identification of the corresponding regions across all frames, the mobile terminal applies a predetermined processing operation to the remaining areas—that is, the areas outside the selected region—or alternatively, to the selected regions themselves, depending on the desired editing outcome. This predetermined processing may include, without limitation, blurring, pixelation, masking, color adjustment, sharpening, or other image enhancement or obscuration techniques. The processing is applied consistently across all frames, ensuring uniform treatment of the designated regions throughout the entire multimedia sequence.

After the processing operation has been completed for all frames, the mobile terminal proceeds to encode the modified picture frames back into a cohesive multimedia file. Critically, this encoding process preserves the original time parameters associated with each frame, ensuring that the newly generated multimedia file maintains the same playback duration, frame rate, and temporal synchronization as the original file. This preservation of timing information ensures that the resulting output file remains fully compatible with standard playback systems and retains the intended viewing experience, notwithstanding the modifications made to specific regions within the content.

## Detailed Description

In one exemplary embodiment, the mobile terminal comprises a decoding module configured to receive an input multimedia file and decode it into a sequence of picture frames, each frame being associated with a corresponding timestamp or time parameter indicating its position within the playback sequence. The decoding module may support various multimedia formats and codecs commonly used in mobile terminal applications, ensuring broad compatibility with content sourced from different capture devices or downloaded from various content providers.

The mobile terminal further comprises a display unit configured to present one or more of the decoded picture frames to the user. In certain embodiments, the display unit presents an initial frame—which may be the first frame of the sequence or any other frame selected by default or by the user—upon which the user can perform the region selection operation. The display unit may incorporate a touch-sensitive screen or other interactive display technology to facilitate intuitive region selection.

A selection receiving module is configured to detect and interpret user input corresponding to the desired region within the displayed frame. This module may support various selection modalities, including but not limited to freehand drawing to outline an irregular region, geometric shape selection (such as rectangles, circles, or polygons), or point-based selection where the user taps on an object of interest and the system automatically determines the boundaries of that object using image segmentation techniques.

Once the region has been selected in the reference frame, an identification module analyzes the remaining picture frames to locate the corresponding region in each frame. In some embodiments, this identification module employs feature-based tracking algorithms that identify distinctive visual characteristics within the selected region—such as edges, corners, color histograms, or texture patterns—and searches for these same characteristics in subsequent and preceding frames. In other embodiments, the identification module may utilize motion estimation techniques, optical flow analysis, or machine learning-based object detection and tracking models to achieve robust region identification even in the presence of complex motion, occlusion, or lighting changes.

A processing module then applies the predetermined processing operation to the identified regions or the areas surrounding them, according to the configuration selected by the user or predefined by the system. The predetermined processing may be customizable, allowing the user to select from a menu of available processing options, such as varying degrees of blur intensity, different masking patterns, or specific color filters. In some embodiments, the processing module may also allow the user to apply different processing operations to different regions within the same frame, or to adjust the processing parameters dynamically based on the characteristics of the tracked region.

Finally, an encoding module reassembles the processed picture frames into a new multimedia file, incorporating the original time parameters extracted during the initial decoding step. This ensures that the new file maintains synchronization with any associated audio tracks and preserves the intended playback characteristics of the original content. The resulting multimedia file can then be stored on the mobile terminal, shared with other devices, or uploaded to various platforms, with the selectively processed regions remaining consistent throughout the entire duration of the video.

## Advantages of the Disclosed Approach

The method and mobile terminal disclosed herein offer several significant advantages over conventional multimedia editing approaches. First, by requiring the user to select a region of interest only once—rather than in every individual frame—the disclosed technique dramatically reduces the time and effort required to perform region-specific editing tasks, making such editing accessible even to users with limited technical expertise. Second, the automatic identification of corresponding regions across frames ensures a high degree of consistency and accuracy in the applied processing, avoiding the jitter, misalignment, or inconsistency that might result from manual frame-by-frame editing. Third, by preserving the original time parameters during the encoding process, the disclosed method ensures that the resulting multimedia file remains fully compatible with standard playback systems and retains the original viewing experience, aside from the intended modifications.

These advantages make the disclosed technique particularly well-suited for a variety of practical applications, including but not limited to privacy protection in videos containing sensitive or personally identifiable information, content censorship or moderation, artistic enhancement of specific subjects within a video, and highlighting or emphasizing particular elements of interest for educational, promotional, or entertainment purposes. The efficient, automated nature of the disclosed approach makes it especially valuable for implementation on mobile terminals, where computational resources and user attention span may be more limited compared to desktop editing environments, yet where the demand for quick and effective content editing continues to grow alongside the increasing use of mobile devices for multimedia capture and sharing.

counterfactuals.output:
# PATENT DISCLOSURE SUMMARY

**Title:** Method and Apparatus for Region-Selective Video Privacy Processing on a Mobile Terminal

---

## FIELD OF THE INVENTION

The present disclosure relates to mobile terminal video processing, and more particularly to systems and methods for identifying, tracking, and preserving a user-selected region of interest across all frames of a video sequence while applying obfuscation (blurring, pixelation, or masking) to the remaining frame content, followed by re-encoding into an output video file.

---

## BACKGROUND

Mobile terminals (smartphones, tablets, wearable devices) are increasingly used to capture video in environments containing sensitive, private, or extraneous visual information—bystanders, background documents, license plates, screens, or proprietary equipment. Existing solutions typically require desktop-grade software, apply blurring uniformly across an entire scene, or demand frame-by-frame manual editing, which is impractical on resource-constrained mobile hardware and burdensome for average users.

There exists a need for an on-device method that allows a user to select a single region of interest (ROI) in a reference frame, have that ROI automatically tracked and preserved throughout the entire video, and have all remaining content processed to obscure identifying detail—without requiring cloud processing or specialized editing skills.

---

## SUMMARY OF THE INVENTION

The disclosed invention provides a mobile terminal-implemented method comprising:

1. **Video Ingestion**: Receiving or capturing a source video file comprising a plurality of sequential frames.

2. **Region Selection Interface**: Presenting a user interface on a touchscreen display enabling a user to select a region of interest via touch gestures (e.g., bounding box, freehand outline, tap-to-select object) on a representative frame (first frame, key frame, or any user-designated frame).

3. **Region Tracking Module**: Employing an on-device tracking algorithm (e.g., optical flow, feature-point tracking, or a lightweight neural object-tracking model) to propagate the selected ROI coordinates across all subsequent and/or preceding frames of the video, accounting for object motion, camera movement, scale changes, and partial occlusion.

4. **Adaptive Mask Generation**: Generating, for each frame, a binary or feathered mask distinguishing the tracked ROI from the remaining frame area, with optional edge-smoothing to reduce visual artifacts at the ROI boundary.

5. **Selective Obfuscation Engine**: Applying one or more configurable obfuscation techniques (Gaussian blur, pixelation, solid color masking, or generative inpainting) to all frame regions outside the tracked ROI, while leaving pixel data within the ROI unmodified or minimally processed.

6. **Frame Reconstruction**: Recompositing each processed frame by merging the untouched ROI content with the obfuscated background per the generated mask.

7. **Video Re-encoding**: Encoding the sequence of reconstructed frames into a new output video file using a standard or user-selected codec (e.g., H.264, H.265/HEVC, AV1), preserving original resolution, frame rate, and audio track, and storing the output as a distinct file separate from the source video.

8. **Optional Metadata Handling**: Optionally stripping or modifying embedded metadata (GPS, timestamps, device identifiers) in the output file to further enhance privacy.

---

## BRIEF DESCRIPTION OF DRAWINGS (Representative)

- **FIG. 1** — System block diagram of the mobile terminal, including camera module, display/touch input, processor, tracking engine, obfuscation engine, and encoder.
- **FIG. 2** — Flowchart of the end-to-end method from video ingestion to output file generation.
- **FIG. 3** — Example UI screens showing ROI selection via bounding box/freehand tool.
- **FIG. 4** — Illustration of per-frame mask propagation across a sequence with a moving subject.
- **FIG. 5** — Before/after frame comparison showing preserved ROI and blurred background.

---

## DETAILED DESCRIPTION (Key Embodiments)

### A. Region Selection Modalities
- Bounding-box drag selection
- Freehand/lasso selection
- Tap-to-select via semantic segmentation (auto-detecting object boundaries, e.g., a face, product, or document, at the tap location)
- Multi-region selection (optionally preserving multiple ROIs simultaneously)

### B. Tracking Engine Embodiments
- **Optical-flow-based tracking** for lightweight, low-latency propagation on mobile CPUs.
- **Neural tracker (e.g., Siamese network or correlation filter-based)** for robustness to occlusion, deformation, and re-entry into frame.
- **Hybrid approach**: keyframe re-detection combined with inter-frame optical flow to correct drift.
- **Failure handling**: prompting the user to reconfirm ROI location if tracking confidence falls below a threshold, or applying interpolation between manually corrected keyframes.

### C. Obfuscation Techniques
- Variable-intensity Gaussian blur (adjustable radius)
- Pixelation with adjustable block size
- Solid/opaque masking
- Edge feathering to blend ROI boundary naturally
- Optional generative inpainting to replace background with synthetic, non-identifying content

### D. On-Device Processing Optimization
- Utilization of mobile GPU/NPU (Neural Processing Unit) acceleration for real-time or near-real-time tracking and blurring.
- Frame batching and parallel processing pipelines to manage battery and thermal constraints.
- Option for background/asynchronous processing with progress notification.

### E. Output Management
- Original video file remains unaltered and stored separately (non-destructive editing).
- New video file generated with user-configurable filename, resolution, and compression settings.
- Optional preview/scrubbing interface allowing the user to verify ROI tracking accuracy before final export.

---

## EXEMPLARY CLAIMS (Illustrative, Non-Limiting)

**Claim 1.** A method performed by a mobile terminal, comprising: receiving a source video comprising a plurality of frames; receiving, via a touchscreen interface, a user selection defining a region of interest in at least one frame; tracking the region of interest across the plurality of frames using an on-device tracking algorithm; generating, for each frame, a mask distinguishing the region of interest from a remaining region; applying an obfuscation process to the remaining region of each frame while preserving the region of interest; and encoding the processed frames into a new video file distinct from the source video.

**Claim 2.** The method of claim 1, wherein the tracking algorithm comprises an optical flow algorithm, a neural object tracker, or a hybrid combination thereof.

**Claim 3.** The method of claim 1, wherein the obfuscation process comprises at least one of Gaussian blurring, pixelation, solid-color masking, or generative inpainting.

**Claim 4.** The method of claim 1, further comprising detecting a tracking confidence score and prompting the user to reconfirm the region of interest when the confidence score is below a predetermined threshold.

**Claim 5.** The method of claim 1, further comprising stripping or modifying metadata associated with the source video prior to encoding the new video file.

**Claim 6.** A mobile terminal comprising a processor, a touchscreen display, and a non-transitory memory storing instructions that, when executed, cause the processor to perform the method of claim 1.

---

## ADVANTAGES

- Enables fully on-device privacy-preserving video editing without cloud dependency.
- Reduces manual editing burden through automated cross-frame ROI tracking.
- Preserves subject clarity/identifiability where desired while anonymizing surrounding content.
- Adaptable to multiple use cases: personal privacy, content moderation, legal/compliance redaction, journalism, and social media sharing.

---

## INDUSTRIAL APPLICABILITY

The invention is applicable to consumer mobile devices, video editing applications, security/compliance tools, journalism and content-creation platforms, and enterprise mobile applications requiring automated redaction of sensitive visual information in user-generated video content.

---

*This disclosure summary is intended as a preliminary technical description for patent counsel review and does not constitute a final claim set. Additional embodiments, drawings, and claim refinement should be developed in consultation with a registered patent attorney prior to filing.*

# ABSTRACT

A system and method for editing multimedia files based on region tracking across multiple frames is disclosed. The system comprises a decoding unit configured to receive and decode a multimedia file into a plurality of sequential frames, each frame comprising image data associated with a temporal position within the multimedia file. The system further comprises one or more processing units communicatively coupled to the decoding unit, the processing units configured to receive a user-selected area corresponding to a region of interest within a first frame of the plurality of sequential frames, the selected area defined by a set of boundary coordinates. The processing units are further configured to analyze image characteristics within the selected area, including at least one of pixel color values, edge features, and motion vectors, and to track the selected area across each subsequent frame of the plurality of sequential frames by identifying corresponding regions based on the analyzed image characteristics, thereby generating a tracked area for each frame corresponding to the user-selected area of the first frame. The processing units are additionally configured to apply at least one editing operation selectively to the tracked area in each frame, the editing operation comprising at least one of a visual effect, a color adjustment, a blurring operation, a masking operation, and an object replacement, while substantially preserving image data outside the tracked area unmodified. The system further comprises an encoding unit configured to receive the plurality of frames having the editing operation applied to the tracked area and to encode the plurality of frames into an edited multimedia file. The tracking performed by the processing units accommodates changes in position, scale, and orientation of the selected area across the plurality of sequential frames, enabling consistent application of the editing operation notwithstanding motion of a subject or region corresponding to the selected area. The system may further comprise a display unit configured to present the multimedia file and to receive the user-selected area via a user input device. Advantageously, the disclosed system enables efficient and consistent editing of a specific region across an entire multimedia file without requiring frame-by-frame manual selection, thereby reducing processing time and computational resources while improving accuracy of localized multimedia editing.

# Technical Disclosure: Video Privacy Masking System for Mobile Devices

## Field of the Invention

This disclosure relates to systems and methods for applying privacy masking to video content captured or stored on mobile devices, and more particularly to techniques for selectively obscuring sensitive regions within video frames while preserving original encoding characteristics and temporal metadata.

## Background

Mobile devices increasingly serve as primary tools for capturing video content in contexts where privacy concerns arise—including recording of license plates, faces, documents, screens, or other identifying information. Existing solutions for video redaction typically require desktop-class processing resources, cloud-based services (which introduce privacy and latency concerns of their own), or produce output files with altered timing characteristics that create playback synchronization issues or incompatibility with downstream editing tools. There exists a need for an on-device solution capable of decoding video, enabling precise user-directed or automated region selection, tracking that region's position across frames despite motion, and re-encoding the result while preserving the original video's timing metadata to ensure compatibility and synchronization fidelity.

## Summary of the Invention

The invention provides a method and system for applying privacy masks to designated regions within a video file on a mobile device, comprising the following operative stages:

### 1. Video Decoding Stage

The system receives an input video file in a compressed format (e.g., H.264, H.265/HEVC, or VP9) and utilizes a hardware- or software-based decoder native to the mobile device's operating system (e.g., platform-provided media codec frameworks) to decode the compressed bitstream into a sequence of uncompressed frames. During decoding, the system extracts and retains the original container-level and stream-level timing metadata, including but not limited to:

- Presentation timestamps (PTS) for each frame
- Decode timestamps (DTS) where applicable
- Frame rate and time base information
- Key frame (I-frame) positions within the group-of-pictures (GOP) structure
- Original bitrate and codec profile parameters

This metadata is stored in a temporary buffer or data structure associated with the decoding session, indexed by frame number, for later use during the re-encoding stage.

### 2. Area Selection Stage

The system presents a user interface allowing selection of one or more regions within a reference frame (e.g., the first frame, a user-scrubbed frame, or an automatically detected frame containing sensitive content). Selection may be accomplished through one or more of the following mechanisms:

- **Manual selection**: touch-based drawing of bounding boxes, freeform shapes, or polygon vertices directly on the displayed frame
- **Automated detection**: application of on-device machine learning models (e.g., object detection or classification networks trained to identify faces, license plates, text, or screens) to propose candidate regions, which may be accepted, adjusted, or rejected by the user
- **Hybrid selection**: a combination wherein automated detection proposes initial bounding regions and manual touch input refines the boundaries

The selected region is represented internally as a set of coordinates (e.g., normalized x/y bounding box corners, or a mask polygon) associated with the reference frame index.

### 3. Region Identification and Tracking Across Frames

Once a region is selected in a reference frame, the system employs a tracking mechanism to identify and follow the corresponding region across the remaining frames of the video sequence, accommodating motion of the camera, the subject, or both. Tracking may utilize one or more of the following techniques, alone or in combination:

- **Optical flow estimation** between consecutive frames to propagate region coordinates forward and/or backward in time
- **Feature-based tracking** (e.g., keypoint detection and matching) to maintain lock on the selected region despite scale, rotation, or perspective changes
- **ML-based object tracking models** (e.g., correlation filter trackers or lightweight neural tracking networks optimized for on-device/mobile inference) that output updated bounding coordinates per frame
- **Interpolation/extrapolation** between sparsely tracked keyframes to reduce per-frame computational cost, with confidence scoring to flag frames requiring re-detection or manual correction

For each frame in the sequence, the system generates an updated set of mask coordinates, stored in association with the corresponding frame index and original timestamp extracted in Stage 1. The system may additionally apply temporal smoothing (e.g., low-pass filtering of coordinate trajectories) to reduce jitter in the applied mask across consecutive frames.

### 4. Mask Application

For each frame, the system applies a privacy-preserving transformation to the pixel data within the tracked region. Transformation techniques may include, without limitation:

- Gaussian or box blur
- Pixelation/mosaic effect
- Solid color fill or opaque overlay
- Edge-feathering to blend the masked region boundary with surrounding unmasked content

### 5. Re-encoding Stage

The modified (masked) frame sequence is passed to an encoder for reconstruction into an output compressed video file. Critically, the encoder is configured using the original timing metadata retained from Stage 1, such that:

- Each output frame is assigned the same presentation timestamp as its corresponding input frame
- The original frame rate and time base are preserved
- Key frame positions are aligned with the original GOP structure where feasible, to minimize seek/scrubbing artifacts
- Audio streams, if present, are passed through or re-multiplexed without alteration, remaining synchronized to the original timestamps

This ensures that the output video file exhibits playback duration, frame timing, and audio/video synchronization identical to the source file, despite the intervening decode-mask-encode pipeline, and remains compatible with standard media players and editing tools without requiring timestamp correction.

## Illustrative System Architecture

A representative implementation comprises:

- A **Decoder Module** interfacing with the mobile OS's native media framework
- A **Metadata Cache** for temporary storage of extracted timing information
- A **Selection UI Module** for rendering frames and capturing user input
- A **Detection Module** (optional) incorporating on-device ML inference for automated region proposal
- A **Tracking Module** implementing optical flow, feature-matching, and/or ML-based tracking algorithms
- A **Mask Rendering Module** applying the chosen obscuring effect to tracked regions per frame
- An **Encoder Module** reconstructing the output file using cached metadata to restore original timing characteristics

## Alternative Embodiments

- The tracking module may operate in a background/asynchronous mode, processing the full video for region trajectories prior to presenting a preview, or in a streaming/incremental mode that processes and previews frames as tracking completes.
- Multiple independently tracked regions may be masked simultaneously within a single video, each with independently configured mask types.
- The system may support re-selection or correction of tracked regions at any frame, with propagation of corrections forward and/or backward through the sequence.
- Metadata preservation may extend to container-level metadata (e.g., rotation flags, color space information, HDR metadata) in addition to timing information.
- The system may operate entirely on-device to avoid transmission of sensitive video content to external servers, or may optionally offload computationally intensive tracking/detection stages to a paired or cloud-based system while retaining decode/encode operations on-device.

## Advantages

The disclosed approach enables privacy-preserving video redaction to be performed entirely on resource-constrained mobile hardware while (a) maintaining perfect timing fidelity with the source file, (b) supporting both manual and automated workflows for region selection, and (c) robustly tracking regions of interest across frames despite motion, thereby avoiding the flicker, drift, or manual frame-by-frame masking burden associated with naive implementations.

# PATENT APPLICATION

## TITLE OF THE INVENTION
**INFORMATION PROCESSING METHOD AND MOBILE TERMINAL FOR REGION-SELECTIVE VIDEO PROCESSING**

---

## FIELD OF THE INVENTION

The present disclosure relates to the field of video processing technology, and more particularly, to an information processing method and a mobile terminal capable of decoding a video, receiving a user-selected region of interest within a reference frame, propagating the region identification information across multiple video frames, applying image processing operations to areas outside the selected region, and encoding a processed output video.

---

## BACKGROUND OF THE INVENTION

With the proliferation of mobile terminals equipped with cameras and video-capture capabilities, users increasingly demand the ability to selectively edit or process portions of recorded video content. Conventional video editing solutions typically require frame-by-frame manual selection of regions of interest, which is time-consuming, computationally expensive, and impractical for real-time or near-real-time processing on resource-constrained mobile devices.

Existing solutions often apply uniform processing (such as blurring, mosaicking, color adjustment, or filtering effects) across an entire video frame, without providing users the ability to preserve a specific region of interest (e.g., a face, a product, or a subject of focus) while modifying the remainder of the frame content. Furthermore, conventional systems that do offer selective region processing generally lack efficient mechanisms for propagating a single user-defined selection across an entire video sequence, resulting in inefficient use of processing resources and degraded user experience, particularly on mobile terminals with limited computational power and battery life.

There is, therefore, a need for an improved information processing method and mobile terminal that allows a user to define a region of interest once, within a single frame, and have that selection efficiently propagated and applied throughout the video, with processing operations selectively applied to non-selected regions, followed by efficient re-encoding of the resulting video.

---

## SUMMARY OF THE INVENTION

The present disclosure provides an information processing method and a mobile terminal that address the aforementioned deficiencies in the prior art. In accordance with various embodiments, the disclosed method comprises the following operations:

1. **Decoding** a source video to obtain a plurality of video frames, each frame comprising image data corresponding to a particular time instant within the video sequence.

2. **Displaying** at least one frame, herein referred to as a reference frame or first frame, to a user via a display unit of the mobile terminal, and **receiving a user input** indicative of a selected region within the reference frame. The selected region may correspond to any arbitrary shape, including but not limited to rectangular, circular, polygonal, or freeform regions, and may be defined via touch input, stylus input, gesture input, or any other suitable input mechanism supported by the mobile terminal.

3. **Generating region identification information** corresponding to the user-selected region, wherein the region identification information comprises data sufficient to identify the location, shape, size, and/or boundary of the selected region within the reference frame. In certain embodiments, the region identification information may further comprise feature data extracted from the selected region (e.g., feature points, color histograms, edge information, or object recognition data) to facilitate accurate propagation across subsequent frames.

4. **Determining corresponding regions** in a plurality of other frames of the video (i.e., frames other than the reference frame) based on the region identification information. In some embodiments, this determination is performed using object tracking algorithms, optical flow estimation, feature matching, or other motion-compensation techniques known in the art, such that the selected region is accurately tracked and mapped across frames despite changes in position, scale, rotation, or perspective of the corresponding subject matter within the video.

5. **Applying at least one image processing operation** to a portion of each frame located outside the corresponding region (i.e., the complementary region), while leaving the corresponding region itself substantially unprocessed, or subjecting it to a different, second image processing operation. Non-limiting examples of the image processing operation include blurring, mosaic/pixelation processing, color/tone adjustment, brightness/contrast adjustment, noise addition or reduction, filter application, watermarking, and/or object replacement.

6. **Encoding** the plurality of processed frames to generate a new (target) video file, using any suitable video encoding standard (e.g., H.264, H.265/HEVC, VP9, AV1, or similar).

In some embodiments, the mobile terminal comprises a decoding module, a display module, a receiving module, a determination module, a processing module, and an encoding module, each configured to perform corresponding operations of the disclosed method. The mobile terminal may further comprise a memory, a processor, and a communication interface configured to store, execute, and transmit/receive data associated with the disclosed method.

Advantageously, the disclosed embodiments allow a user to define a region of interest in only a single frame, rather than requiring frame-by-frame manual selection, thereby significantly reducing the computational burden, processing time, and power consumption associated with region-selective video processing on a mobile terminal. Additionally, by propagating region identification information using tracking or feature-matching techniques rather than requiring per-frame manual input, the disclosed method improves both processing efficiency and user experience.

## DETAILED DESCRIPTION OF THE EMBODIMENTS

Reference will now be made in detail to various embodiments, examples of which are illustrated in the accompanying drawings. While the disclosure will be described in conjunction with specific embodiments, it is understood that the description is not intended to limit the disclosure to those embodiments. On the contrary, the disclosure is intended to cover alternatives, modifications, and equivalents as may be included within the spirit and scope of the disclosure as defined by the appended claims.

### 1. Overview of the Method

Referring to FIG. 1, an information processing method 100 is illustrated, comprising the following steps.

**Step S101: Decoding a Source Video**

A mobile terminal obtains a source video, which may be captured locally via a camera module of the mobile terminal, retrieved from local storage, or received via a network from a remote source (e.g., a server or another terminal device). The mobile terminal decodes the source video using a decoder corresponding to the encoding format of the source video (e.g., an H.264 decoder, H.265 decoder, or other suitable decoder), to obtain a sequence of decoded video frames, each comprising pixel data representative of an image at a corresponding point in time.

**Step S102: Displaying a Reference Frame and Receiving a Region Selection**

At least one frame of the decoded video frames, designated as a reference frame, is displayed to the user via a touch-sensitive display or other display unit of the mobile terminal. The mobile terminal receives, via a user interface, a user input designating a region within the reference frame. 

In some embodiments, the reference frame is the first frame of the video; in other embodiments, the reference frame may be a user-selected frame at an arbitrary temporal position within the video, or a frame automatically selected based on image quality metrics, scene detection, or other criteria.

The user input may take multiple forms, including but not limited to: (a) a touch gesture tracing the boundary of the desired region; (b) a tap-and-drag gesture defining a bounding box or bounding shape; (c) a tap input selecting a pre-identified object or face within the frame (e.g., via object detection or facial recognition preprocessing); or (d) a multi-touch gesture defining a polygonal region via multiple touch points.

**Step S103: Generating Region Identification Information**

Upon receiving the user's region selection, the mobile terminal generates region identification information corresponding to the selected region. In some embodiments, this region identification information comprises coordinate data defining the boundary of the selected region (e.g., a set of vertex coordinates, a center point and radius, or a bounding box defined by corner coordinates). In other embodiments, the region identification information further comprises extracted feature data corresponding to image content within the selected region, such as feature points (e.g., SIFT, SURF, ORB, or other feature descriptors), color distribution data, texture data, or semantic labels (e.g., "face," "license plate," "product label") obtained via a trained recognition model.

**Step S104: Determining Corresponding Regions in Other Frames**

The mobile terminal determines, for each of a plurality of other frames within the decoded video (i.e., frames other than the reference frame), a corresponding region that corresponds to the user-selected region in the reference frame. This determination may be performed using one or more of the following non-limiting techniques:

- **Object tracking**: applying a tracking algorithm (e.g., a correlation filter tracker, Kalman filter, mean-shift tracker, or deep-learning-based tracker) initialized using the region identification information from the reference frame, to track the corresponding region across subsequent (and/or preceding) frames.

- **Optical flow estimation**: computing pixel-wise or block-wise motion vectors between consecutive frames, and applying the computed motion vectors to propagate the boundary of the selected region from the reference frame to other frames.

- **Feature matching**: extracting feature points from each of the plurality of other frames, and matching such feature points against the feature data associated with the selected region in the reference frame, to identify a corresponding region in each frame.

- **Object recognition/re-detection**: applying an object detection or recognition model to each of the plurality of other frames to re-detect the semantic object or content type corresponding to the selected region (e.g., re-detecting a face across frames using a face detector).

It is understood that the plurality of other frames may include frames temporally subsequent to the reference frame, frames temporally prior to the reference frame, or both, such that the corresponding region is propagated bidirectionally throughout the video sequence.

**Step S105: Applying an Image Processing Operation to a Region Outside the Corresponding Region**

For each frame among the plurality of frames (including, in some embodiments, the reference frame itself), the mobile terminal applies at least one image processing operation to the portion of the frame located outside the corresponding region (i.e., the complementary region of the frame). In some embodiments, the selected/corresponding region remains unmodified, thereby preserving the visual content of the selected region while altering the remainder of the frame. In other embodiments, a second, different image processing operation is applied to the selected/corresponding region, distinct from the operation applied to the complementary region.

Non-limiting examples of image processing operations include:

- Mosaic/pixelation processing of the complementary region;
- Color desaturation, grayscale conversion, or color-tone adjustment of the complementary region;

- Addition of a stylistic filter or artistic effect;
- Overlaying a watermark, graphic, or text within the complementary region;

# TECHNICAL SUMMARY

## FIELD OF THE INVENTION

The present disclosure relates to a mobile terminal system and method for multimedia signal processing, and more particularly, to a system enabling selective region-based decoding, tracking, and re-encoding of multimedia content while preserving temporal synchronization parameters.

---

## BACKGROUND

Conventional mobile multimedia processing systems typically apply uniform processing operations (e.g., blurring, masking, compression, filtering) across an entire video frame sequence. Such approaches lack the capability to selectively identify a region of interest (ROI) in a single reference frame and propagate corresponding region detection across a plurality of subsequent or preceding frames, while independently processing non-selected regions and preserving original timing metadata upon re-encoding. There exists a need for a mobile terminal-based system capable of efficient, user-directed, region-specific multimedia processing suitable for resource-constrained devices.

---

## SUMMARY OF THE INVENTION

An embodiment of the present invention provides a mobile terminal system comprising:

1. **A decoding module**, configured to receive an encoded multimedia file and decode said file into a plurality of sequential picture frames, each frame associated with a corresponding time parameter (e.g., presentation timestamp, decoding timestamp, or frame index).

2. **A user interface module**, configured to display at least one reference frame among the plurality of decoded frames and to receive a user input designating a selected area within said reference frame, the selected area defined by boundary coordinates, a geometric shape, or a user-drawn contour.

3. **An area detection module**, configured to:
   - Extract feature characteristics (e.g., color histogram, edge information, texture descriptors, or motion vectors) of the selected area in the reference frame;
   - Apply an area tracking algorithm (e.g., block matching, optical flow estimation, or feature-point correspondence) to detect a corresponding area in each of the other decoded frames, said corresponding area exhibiting positional and/or shape variation relative to the reference frame due to inter-frame motion.

4. **A processing module**, configured to apply at least one image processing operation selectively to the non-selected area (i.e., the region outside the detected corresponding area) in each frame, wherein said operation includes, without limitation, blurring, pixelation, masking, color conversion, resolution reduction, or object removal, while the selected/detected area remains substantially unprocessed or is subjected to a different processing operation.

5. **An encoding module**, configured to re-encode the plurality of processed frames into a new multimedia file, wherein the time parameter originally associated with each frame is preserved and embedded into the new file such that playback timing, frame rate, and synchronization with any associated audio track remain consistent with the original multimedia file.

---

## DETAILED DESCRIPTION (EXEMPLARY EMBODIMENT)

### System Architecture

The mobile terminal (e.g., smartphone, tablet, or portable media device) comprises a processor, memory, display, user input interface (touchscreen, stylus, or pointing device), and a multimedia codec (hardware or software-based).

### Operational Flow

**Step 1 – Decoding:**
The multimedia file (e.g., MP4, AVI, or proprietary container format) is received and decoded into individual frames F₁, F₂, ..., Fₙ, each tagged with time parameter T₁, T₂, ..., Tₙ.

**Step 2 – Area Selection:**
A reference frame Fₖ is displayed on the terminal's display. The user selects an area A_k via touch input, defining a bounding region (rectangular, elliptical, or freeform polygon).

**Step 3 – Area Detection Across Frames:**
The area detection module computes a correspondence mapping between A_k and areas A₁, A₂, ..., A_{k-1}, A_{k+1}, ..., Aₙ in the remaining frames. This may be achieved through:
- (a) Motion vector extraction from the original encoded bitstream (if available), reducing computational overhead;
- (b) Feature-based tracking (e.g., SIFT, SURF, ORB) applied across frames;
- (c) Optical flow-based dense correspondence estimation.

**Step 4 – Selective Processing:**
For each frame Fᵢ, the region outside the corresponding detected area Aᵢ (i.e., the complement region) is subjected to the designated processing operation, while area Aᵢ is preserved in its original or minimally altered state. This enables applications such as privacy masking (blurring backgrounds while preserving a subject's face), region-specific compression, or selective visual effects.

**Step 5 – Re-encoding with Time Parameter Preservation:**
The processed frames are re-encoded using an encoder module. Each frame's original time parameter Tᵢ is retained and written into the header/metadata of the new encoded file, ensuring that the resultant multimedia file maintains identical playback duration, frame timing, and audio-video synchronization as the source file.

---

## ADVANTAGES

- Enables computationally efficient, localized processing suitable for mobile terminals with limited processing power and battery capacity.
- Preserves temporal integrity of the original multimedia content, avoiding synchronization drift.
- Provides user-directed control over region selection without requiring frame-by-frame manual re-selection.
- Supports a variety of tracking algorithms adaptable to different content types (static background, moving subject, dynamic scene).

---

## CLAIMS (ILLUSTRATIVE)

1. A method for processing multimedia data in a mobile terminal, comprising: decoding an encoded multimedia file into a plurality of frames each having an associated time parameter; displaying a reference frame among said plurality of frames; receiving a user input selecting an area within said reference frame; detecting a corresponding area in each of the other frames of said plurality of frames based on said selected area; applying a processing operation to an area other than said detected corresponding area in each of said frames; and encoding the processed frames into a new multimedia file, wherein the time parameter of each frame is preserved in said new multimedia file.

2. The method of claim 1, wherein detecting the corresponding area comprises applying a motion tracking algorithm using at least one of block matching, optical flow, or feature point correspondence.

3. The method of claim 1, wherein the processing operation comprises at least one of blurring, pixelation, masking, or resolution alteration.

4. A mobile terminal system configured to perform the method of claim 1, comprising a decoding module, a user interface module, an area detection module, a processing module, and an encoding module.
